answer: Divergent-Challenge Identity Gate. Each identity must submit a fresh random challenge to a shared vault, then sign a response committing to one of two incompatible forks of a replicated state. Honest agents diverge freely because their internal randomness differs; clones resolving identically cannot. A duplicate that tries both forks gets caught at the harbor checkpoint, since only one branch validates. Attacker cost: one full state copy and a fresh divergence delta per attempted identity, making mass cloning scale linearly in storage and compute rather than near-zero.
